newsitem.title: USA: Viacom seeks public auction of USA Networks.
newsitem.headline: Viacom seeks public auction of USA Networks.

text.p: Viacom Inc. on Monday asked a judge to hold a public auction of USA Networks, the cable television partnership jointly owned with Seagram Co. Ltd. According to court documents filed Monday, Viacom opted for
the auction after its offer to buy Seagram's half of the partnership for $1.94 billion was rejected by the Candian beverage and entertainment company on June 12.

Viacom -- which owns the Paramount Pictures movie studio and the MTV and Nickelodeon cable TV networks -- and Seagram, which owns entertainment and theme park concern Universal Inc., have been fighting for control of USA Network, with each side accusing the other of violating the terms of the partnership agreement.

In its own filing, Seagram said last month's Delaware Chancery Court finding that Viacom had violated a non-compete provision of the partnership means that Viacom is obliged to sell its share under a buy-sell provision that could prove disadvantageous to New York-based Viacom.

Seagram sued Viacom last year, charging the company with violating the terms of the partnership agreement by launching a new cable channel called Nick at Nite TV Land. Montreal-based Seagram said the partnership prevents either company from operating or launching entertainment cable networks outside of the USA Network.
However, Viacom contends there is no breach of the partnership, that the partnership is working well and that Universal is trying to get control of USA Network "at an unfairly low price."

The buy-sell provision would allow Seagram either to sell its share to Viacom at the high end of a valuation range or buy Viacom's share at the low end. The range would be the difference between Viacom's estimate of the partnership's worth and the estimate of an independent investment banker.

Seagram also wants Delaware Vice Chancellor Myron Steele to order Viacom to dispose of its cable networks or to stop operating them unless, by some unspecified date, Viacom agrees to trigger the buy-sell provision and abide by it. According to Seagram, the order would remedy Viacom's breach of the non-compete provision.
